gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Expressive and a bit showy, Tektur looks ruled and compassed into place, every curve cleanly opened at its ends. Noto Sans Ogham follows in a plain sans with tall, bold-looking lowercase, giving the page a sturdy floor under all that drawing.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-ol-chiki: Tektur is all pipe-cleaner strokes, smooth and unpinched, with no swelling bowls anywhere. Noto Sans Ol Chiki holds its curve tails back and packs words into solid blocks, which is the pair's strongest quality: tidy density against open wire.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-old-hungarian: Noto Sans Old Hungarian reads friendly and wide-mouthed, its tall a, e and s staying legible even tiny. Tektur above it looks bent from a single length of wire, and the two trade loose curves for open ones without any friction.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-old-italic:
Tektur draws everything with one fixed nib, curves wide open at the ends.

Noto Sans Old Italic sits tight between its x-height and capitals, with curve endings kept apart, so a long passage would feel compact, steady and quietly businesslike.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-old-north-ara: Tektur's tube-like strokes look like neon glass bent into letters, with outsized lowercase to match. Noto Sans Old North Arabian then settles into a dense, tall band of text, its terminals flaring outward like tongs, so a long passage would feel packed but approachable.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-old-permic:
Tektur keeps its curves full right through every turn.

It is the one to lean on for expressive, wire-like shapes, while Noto Sans Old Permic does the quieter job, with rounded sans-serif forms open to the side and lowercase nearly matching the capitals.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-old-persian: Every Tektur glyph runs at a single flat line weight, a pipe-cleaner look with outsized lowercase. Noto Sans Old Persian is lofty and tall in the body, its counters breathing into the white space, so a longer read goes down smoothly.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-old-sogdian: Tektur has a blueprint-lettering feel, its constant line and generous curve openings looking drawn rather than set. And Noto Sans Old Sogdian, a sans-serif with tall x-height and wide mouths, stays crisp when shrunk, which is where this pairing is strongest.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-oriya:
Tektur ends every stroke as wide as its middle, like wire.

Noto Sans Oriya, a sans with small letters nearly as tall as its capitals and curve gaps that stay generous, makes a longer stretch read openly and comfortably.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-osage:
Noto Sans Osage reads in puffed-out lowercase bowls and sweeping curves that never close.

Tektur draws every stroke at one thickness, so the pair's strongest quality is how a plain sans with inflated shapes lets that wiry, expressive heading stand out.
